dimensions.summary: The registered consumer set is derived from the package registry, Graph composes canonical Shared contracts, and the nonexistent Model package is explicitly deferred.
Consumer discovery and cycle validation are registry-driven, so later admitted packages use the same policy without a Graph-specific dependency algorithm.
SH4 changes contract ownership and build-time guards without adding a runtime algorithm, traversal or allocation path.
dimensions.justification: The existing status operation performs the same bounded object construction; installed package size remains covered by pack:check.

dimensions.summary: Undeclared Shared deep imports, ambiguous root imports, dependency cycles and premature CLI bridges now fail closed.
The migration processes package metadata and source import specifiers only; it reads no repository content, user path, credential or telemetry data.
dimensions.justification: No new runtime data collection or artifact content is introduced by SH4.

dimensions.summary: Portable path-free package identities and Node APIs pass locally; the Linux, macOS and Windows remote matrix is still required for admission evidence.
Shared remains a zero-runtime-dependency leaf, Graph depends only on Shared, and the central CLI consumes neither development package.
Graph contract references and result envelopes are type-checked, immutable and accepted by the canonical generated Shared validator.
Graph preserves its existing public API while replacing a locally constructed contract reference with the canonical Shared constructor and type.
SH4 adds no long-running operation, external resource or recoverable runtime state; failures are synchronous build-gate failures with actionable paths.
dimensions.justification: Runtime retry, rollback and cancellation behavior is unchanged because no runtime orchestration was introduced.

dimensions.summary: One machine-readable consumer inventory drives a generic boundary guard and focused package conformance tests; no internal package documentation was duplicated.
Independent Shared and Graph tarballs install into an isolated consumer, validate an actual Graph result and retain publication refusal and package allowlists.
